text:
dan: Heads up  I was on a 3-month deployment in the UK and totally missed open enrollment. I just got back and need to add my spouse + stepson. Marriage cert is stuck in the registry and the stepkid's birth cert is in Welsh; what are our options to enroll now?
peopleops-jane: Welcome home! :wave: Marriage is a QLE but you usually have 30 days. Given deployment, we sometimes make exceptions. Tagging @noah-benefits.
noah-benefits: Sorry for the scramble. Short answer: we can do a QLE exception in limited cases like deployment that prevented portal access. We'll need supporting docs (deployment orders or commander letter) + whatever proof you have for spouse/stepchild.
dan: I have my deployment orders and a stamped statement from the base admin. For the documents stuck overseas I can scan the digital receipt from the registry and a certified translation is pending.
noah-benefits: Good. For provisional intake we accept any TWO of the following for each dependent: (1) foreign marriage certificate or registry receipt, (2) passport or provisional travel doc, (3) birth certificate (certified translation if not English), (4) notarized affidavit + deployment/absence proof. If translations are pending, the registry receipt + deployment orders usually let us approve an exception provisionally.
liz: Also toggle dental/vision in the portal separately  those don't auto-add.
payroll-bot: Payroll note: if we make coverage retro to the event date, premiums will be reconciled in the next 1-2 pay runs after benefits processes. That could be a single deduction or a refund. If you want to spread the impact, we can split adjustments across cycles if you email payroll@redwood.example.
dan: Any special handling for the stepchild who lives with my spouse overseas? He's currently on the spouse's passport but doesn't have a US SSN yet.
noah-benefits: That's OK. SSN not required to provisionally enroll; provide SSN within 60 days when available. For dependents living overseas, provide a passport or local birth cert + proof of relationship (birth record showing parent or a sworn affidavit). We'll follow up for final documents and US immigration evidence if needed.
dan: Where do I put everything? I couldn't find the exception flow in the portal.
peopleops-jane: Steps: HR Portal > Benefits > Report a Life Event > Choose: "Add dependent  marriage/stepchild" > Enter event date (use marriage date or return date depending on which you want effective) > Attach: deployment orders + registry receipt + scanned passport page for stepchild > In notes write: "Deployment exception request  unable to access portal while deployed; registry docs pending translation" Or open a case and cc benefits@redwood.example.
benefits-bot: Example note: \"Requesting deployment exception. Deployment dates: 2026-08-01 to 2026-11-30. Marriage date: 2026-10-05. Attached: deployment orders + registry receipt + passport copy. Requesting retro coverage to marriage date.\"
dan: Thanks everyone  uploading docs now and will tag the case number. Appreciate the help.
noah-benefits: Case created: #BEN-90133. We'll review and aim to respond within 3-5 business days; may ask for final translated docs or certified marriage certificate later.
